draft.title: Influences on food choices
card: Many things shape what young people eat. Taste is one: foods a person likes are foods they are more likely to choose, healthy or not.
Cost and convenience matter. Cheap, ready-made food can be easier to buy than fresh food that needs preparing, but fresh food can sometimes be cheaper and quick to prepare.
Family and culture shape habits. Meals at home, traditional foods and religious or cultural practices can support healthy eating or work against it.
Knowledge and commercial factors also play a part. Knowing how to cook and read labels can help, while advertising and special offers can push towards less healthy foods.
draft.remember: Each influence can help or hinder healthy eating, depending on the situation.

a.q: Which example is a cultural influence on a young person's food choices?
opts: Sharing traditional family dishes at festival meals
Buying a snack because it is on special
Choosing a drink because the flavour is sweet
Learning to read a label in a food class
a.why: Traditional dishes shared at festivals come from a cultural background. The special is a cost or commercial influence, sweetness is taste, and learning to read labels is knowledge.

b.q: Lena, 15, lives near a shopping centre and often buys a hot chip pack after school because it is cheap and fast. Which two influences are most at work?
opts: Cost and convenience
Family and culture
Knowledge and taste
Marketing and religion
b.why: The pack is chosen because it is cheap and quick to get. Taste may play a part, but the scenario does not mention flavour, family or advertising.
b.clue: Look at the two reasons given in the scenario.

a.best: Sharing traditional family dishes at festival meals

problems.detail: The clue 'Which example comes from traditions?' gives the answer away. Only one option contains the word 'traditional', so a student can match the word without understanding what a cultural influence is.
